output.methodChoice: Standard-depth EDF analysis (EDF-1). Collected X12 first (churn split by price cohort, connector and seat band, which works as a natural experiment on price), then X7 (connector error logs and engineering notes, for mechanism and the status of the Tallymarsh log). Stopped at the 2-item limit. Items I02 and I04 use only evidence at or before stage S1 (E1–E5).
output.brief:
The rise in cancellations is not a pricing problem; it comes from the Quillbook connection.

Quillbook retired its old invoice interface on 30 March. Since then our connector has dropped or doubled invoices for 1,212 of 1,900 Quillbook-linked accounts. 34% of those have cancelled, against 8% of Quillbook accounts with no recorded failure. Quillbook-linked churn roughly tripled whether or not the price was locked (5.9% vs 6.2%), while accounts without a connector stayed flat at about 1.9%, even though most had the same price rise and app update. Finance's "bigger increase, more churn" pattern reflects that larger accounts use Quillbook more.

Recommend:
- Don't reverse the price: it costs about $220k a month and won't fix this.
- Keep the duplicate-invoice hold; it has kept 3,870 duplicates out of customers' books.
- Make the Quillbook fix (three to four weeks, unscheduled) the top engineering job, and contact every Quillbook-linked account, cancelled ones included, to correct invoices.
- Make the health panel count warning-level events, and raise sync-ticket severity.
- Read the unreviewed Tallymarsh log before any rebuild.

High confidence on Quillbook over price; Tallymarsh and slow support's role remain open.
